newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee quiet vs dollar as RBI stays away.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee quiet vs dollar as RBI stays away.

text.p: The Indian rupee was steady in late morning trade against the dollar in both the forward and spot markets, dealers said.
November delivery dollars were quoted at a premium of 93/95 paise against Wednesday's close of 93/96, they said.
The forex market was largely inactive on Thursday as banks in the commercial capital of Bombay were shut for a local holiday.
Easier domestic liquidity will keep forward premiums down, dealers said.
"Forward premiums should remain soft as call money has eased from Monday's high of around 10.5 percent," a dealer at a state-run bank said.
In the spot market, the rupee was steady in a 35.86/87 per dollar in the absence of Reserve Bank of India (RBI) dollar purchases, dealers said.
RBI dollar buying since Monday, estimated by dealers at around $400-500 million, pushed the rupee down from last weekend's close of 35.745/755.
"They (RBI) are the only buyers in the market at the moment," said a dealer. "So far they haven't bought today and the rupee is stuck in a groove."
In latest deals, the dollar was quoted 35.862/872 rupees.
